selection.retainedCoverage: The earlier V3 receipt/queue/close-fault selections and V4 owner/HTTP/native-store selections are retained without replay or transfer to this changed graph.

implementation.coreDelta: Only accepts the additional OWNED_EXISTING_V4_CUSTODY_QUARANTINE DATA label; queue, receipt, submission observation, stop, counts and close code remain byte-identical.
implementation.bindings: Select the captured actual V4 HTTP client/root with a private default-false persistentCustody flag. Existing public configuration fields and one-shot core fields remain unchanged.
implementation.defaultPaths: V2/V3 public entry functions retain their original flag arguments. No default CLI/runner or operational transport adoption.
implementation.namespaceCompatibility: Two intentional enumerable V4 factory exports are added; not strict module-key-list compatibility. Historical source-pin/export goldens remain unchanged and are not silently weakened or rerun.
implementation.counts: attempted denotes calls to the actual child submit method, not HTTP/network requests or service delivery. A held V4 child can reject that call before any store/transport operation.
implementation.uncertainty: Persistent quarantine prevents fresh HTTP dispatch. A returned owned DB close releases only its module resource slot, never child uncertainty or the persisted marker.
implementation.manualClose: Synchronous admission/queued-next fencing and original cached close Promise are reused. A partial stopped run can reject while its active callback and close finish normally; that is not manufactured custody uncertainty.
implementation.recovery: Existing scoped recovery-state plans remain diagnostic DATA. A declared SUCCEEDED observation does not clear quarantine or authorize payment, signing, dispatch or delivery.
implementation.noNewActions: No create fallback, migration, reset, resend, funding preparation, SDK, signer, verifier, background host or operational helper.

sourceBinding.importClosure: Fourteen authored modules, root package metadata and one selected entry. The existing recovery/model imports are reviewed definition-time dependencies; only the selected state-plan path is invoked.

scenarios.name: borrowed V4 runner stops queued originals after persistent HTTP uncertainty
asserts: The actual borrowed module exposes the explicit V4 factory.
A new V4 store remains borrowed while a three-entry V4 batch completes one fake callback, then receives a 503 and stops before entry three.
Both declared request/response handles close before moving to the next entry or settling failure; at most one fake request is active.
Attempted 2/completed 1/not-attempted 1, queue references 0, one cached rejected close and PERSISTED_UNKNOWN remain distinct.
Same-array receipt reuses the original run Promise; a different array refuses ALREADY_RUN without more requests.

The native store is still usable and funding metadata exact after runner close; queued original is absent. Only the fixture explicitly closes it, then SQL inspects epoch 1 and two exact originals/intents plus one quarantine.

scenarios.name: owned V4 runner preserves partial completion and UNKNOWN after automatic DB release
asserts: The new owned V4 runner opens a second new private V4 file after its synthetic producer closes.
The same three-entry partial/uncertain sequence retains two exact originals/intents, not the queued third.
Run rejects and auto-close remains UNKNOWN while native DB close returns once and the resource slot is RELEASED.
The original run receipt remains cached. After all production handles close, SQL sees epoch 2 and the grant-bound quarantine.

scenarios.name: reopened V4 runner retains reconciliation metadata and dispatches no quarantined batch
asserts: Normal V4 reopen at epoch 3 reads persisted quarantine before any new request.
Scoped keys/state return the exact retained original and POSSIBLY_ATTEMPTED intent with custody uncertainty and NONE authority.
A state-plan initialized with declared INCLUDED/SUCCEEDED still requires RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED and keeps every action/delivery flag false.
One child-submit attempt rejects before new owner/store work: owner counters and actual HTTP request count remain unchanged.
The run and owned close remain rejected; normal DB close/slot release do not reset the marker.
Plan close after root close returns cached detached powerless history; all non-epoch database rows remain exact. This is not process restart.

scenarios.name: manual V4 close stops queued work without manufacturing a grant quarantine
asserts: A separate unquarantined selected grant in the first file starts one active entry while a second remains queued.
Manual close synchronously releases queue references and waits for both declared handles; native store close is not attempted early.
The active callback finishes, root close fulfills and releases its store once, but the partial run rejects CLOSE_REQUESTED.
The runner is not UNKNOWN and performs zero quarantine writes. Only the preexisting other-grant quarantine remains.
A fresh same-grant runner reads NOT_RECORDED and closes without claiming a run. Original/intent rows and all non-epoch metadata stay exact; no queued request is dispatched.

authority.pr193: VALIDATED exact-same-signed-block resend remains distinct from UNKNOWN and ACKNOWLEDGED.

limits: These four source-bound local component cases are not a full queue, HTTP, SQLite, recovery collection, controller, SDK or legacy compatibility suite.
Fake request/response handles and declared proof/status strings establish no sockets, TLS, real proof validity, authenticated backend operation, provider READY or delivery.
Same-process close/reopen is not actual process restart, power loss, fsync/crash qualification or current recovery authority.
The maximum of one active fake request is a selected lifecycle assertion, not a capacity benchmark or production throughput guarantee.
No default/active path is enabled and no original request or signed payment is automatically replayed, replaced or re-signed.
Independent current context, funding, payer/provider/policy authority, real READY, durability, commit/uncertainty and restart/recovery remain separate acceptance gates.
